question:
Refer to the exhibit. An engineer must configure FCoE with these requirements: VLAN 100 must be used to carry the Ethernet traffic; Fabric A must use FCoE on VLAN 11 and VSAN 11; Fabric B must use FCoE on VLAN 12 and VSAN 12; vfc 10 on Fabric A must be bound to Ethernet 1/1 on N5K_1; and vfc 11 on Fabric B must be bound to Ethernet 1/1 on N5K_2. Which interface vfc 10 configuration accomplishes these requirements?
N5K_1(config)# feature fcoe
N5K_1(config)# vlan 100
N5K_1(config)# vsan database
N5K_1(config-vsan-db)# vsan 11

N5K_1(config)# vlan 11
N5K_1(config-vlan)# fcoe vsan 11

N5K_1(config)# vlan 100

N5K_1(config)# interface ethernet 1/1
N5K_1(config-if)# switchport mode trunk
N5K_1(config-if)# switchport trunk allowed vlan 11, 100
N5K_1(config-if)# no shutdown
context: Topology: Fabric A (N5K_1, N5K_2, FCoE VLAN11-VSAN11) and Fabric B (N5K_3, N5K_4, FCoE VLAN12-VSAN12) connect to LAN and SAN clouds and to a C2XX server via Ten1/Ten0.
imageNote: Diagram: Fabric A (N5K_1 e1/1-2, N5K_2) and Fabric B (N5K_3, N5K_4) cross-connect to LAN/SAN clouds, N5K_1-N5K_3 linked via e1/5-6, N5K_2 and N5K_4 both connect down to C2XX server (Ten1/Ten0).
options:
N5K_1(config)# int vfc 10
N5K_1(config-if)# switchport mode sd
N5K_1(config-if)# switchport trunk allowed vsan 11,100
N5K_1(config-if)# bind interface eth 1/1
N5K_1(config-if)# no shutdown

N5K_1(config)# int vfc 10
N5K_1(config-if)# switchport mode e
N5K_1(config-if)# switchport trunk allowed vsan 11
N5K_1(config-if)# bind interface eth 1/1
N5K_1(config-if)# no shutdown

N5K_1(config)# int vfc 10
N5K_1(config-if)# switchport mode f
N5K_1(config-if)# switchport trunk allowed vlan 11,100
N5K_1(config-if)# bind interface eth 1/1
N5K_1(config-if)# no shutdown

N5K_1(config)# int vfc 10
N5K_1(config-if)# switchport mode n
N5K_1(config-if)# switchport trunk allowed vlan 11
N5K_1(config-if)# bind interface eth 1/1
N5K_1(config-if)# no shutdown
theory: FCFs establish FCoE links to each other over VE_Ports (the FCoE equivalent of native FC E ports), so a vfc interface that is really extending the SAN uplink between two FCoE-capable switches, rather than terminating a host's CNA, must be configured with 'switchport mode e', bound to its Ethernet interface, and restricted to the correct fabric's VSAN (11 for Fabric A here); using F, N, or SD mode would be appropriate for a host-facing or SPAN scenario, not a switch-to-switch FCoE extension. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 9 - FCoE Port Types / VE_Port)
